articles.title: Getting to know the app
articles.body:
BALE DOWNLOAD HUB downloads files from allowed public links, checks them, publishes them to your Bale channel and then deletes every temporary file.

  1. Create a Bale bot and copy its token.
  2. Create a channel and make the bot an admin.
  3. Paste the token and channel in the Setup Wizard.
  4. Add links (in the app or by messaging the bot).

Only administrators you define can use the bot.

articles.title: Creating a Bale bot
articles.body:
Bots are created with Bale's official bot-management bot (@botfather inside Bale). Follow the steps in the official documentation: docs.bale.ai.

You choose a name and a username; BotFather then replies with the bot token.

articles.title: Getting and protecting the token
articles.body:
The token looks like 123456789:ABC-DEF.... Anyone who has it controls your bot.

  • Paste it only into the app's token field (it is kept in the Windows Credential Manager, not in the database or in settings files).
  • Never post it in chats or screenshots.
  • If it leaks, ask BotFather to revoke/regenerate it and enter the new one here.

The app masks tokens in logs, error messages, reports and exports.

articles.title: Creating a channel
articles.body: In Bale: New → Channel. A public channel has a username (e.g. @my_files) which is the easiest ID to use.

articles.title: Making the bot a channel admin
articles.body: Open the channel → Administrators → Add admin → choose your bot and allow posting messages. Without this the bot cannot publish and the channel test will fail.

articles.title: Finding the channel ID
articles.body:
Use @username for public channels. The Bale Bot API also accepts the numeric chat id; after a successful test the app shows the numeric ID it received from Bale.

Limit: the documented API has no call to list a bot's channels, so a private channel without a username needs its numeric ID from another source.

articles.title: Finding a user's numeric ID
articles.body: Ask the person to send any message to your bot. If they are not authorised yet, the bot answers with their numeric ID – paste it into Users or into the wizard's admin step.

articles.title: Connection settings
articles.body: Defaults work for most networks. Increase the timeouts on slow connections; set a proxy (http://… or socks5://…) only if Bale is not reachable directly.

articles.title: Testing the connection
articles.body: Use Test next to the token (calls getMe) and next to the channel. The channel test sends a short message and deletes it again – this is the only reliable way to verify posting rights because the Bale API has no 'my permissions' call.

articles.title: Starting and stopping the bot
articles.body: The bot starts automatically when a token is saved and Bot enabled is on (Settings → Bot). Turn it off to stop receiving messages; downloads started from the desktop keep working.

articles.title: Downloading from a link
articles.body: Add links in Downloads → Add links, paste several, or import TXT/CSV. The app analyses each link first (name, size, type) and you confirm. Supported: direct files and pages supported by yt-dlp. Not supported: DRM content, content behind logins/paywalls, private network addresses.

articles.title: Publishing to the channel
articles.body: Images (≤10 MB JPG/PNG) go as photos, MP4 as video, MP3/M4A as audio, everything else as documents. Bale bots can upload at most 50 MB per file. Optionally enable split large files to send 49 MB parts. Scheduling is done by the app (the Bale API has no scheduled posts).

articles.title: Local link API (optional)
articles.body:
Settings → Bot → Enable local link API. Other programs on this computer can then POST links:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1/links -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"urls\":[\"https://example.com/a.pdf\"]}"

It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, needs the key shown in settings, accepts at most 20 links per request, and is off by default.

articles.title: Managing the queue
articles.body: Pause, resume, cancel, retry, change priority, and set concurrent downloads. The queue is saved and restored after a restart or crash; partial downloads resume when the server supports Range requests.

articles.title: Common errors
articles.body:
• Unauthorized / token rejected – wrong or revoked token.
  • Forbidden / not a member – bot is not an admin of the channel.
  • File too large – above your limit or Bale's 50 MB.
  • URL blocked – private/internal address (SSRF protection).
  • Disk space low – the queue pauses automatically.

articles.title: Automatic clean-up
articles.body:
After a successful publish every temporary file of that job (download, processed copy, thumbnail, side files) is deleted; failed or cancelled jobs are cleaned too. Orphans are swept at start-up and on a schedule. Privacy mode also removes the URL and file name from the history.

Honest note: deleting a file is not secure erasure – the operating system may allow recovery with special tools.

articles.title: Managing the database
articles.body: The SQLite database holds only job metadata – never file contents. Use Settings → Backup for integrity check, vacuum and retention.

articles.title: Backups and restore
articles.body: Backups can be password-encrypted. Settings export never contains the token. Restoring first saves a safety copy of the current database.

articles.title: Token security
articles.body: The token is stored in the OS credential vault; if none exists an encrypted file protected by machine/user-derived key is used (stops casual reading, not malware running as you).

articles.title: Installing and updating
articles.body: Run run.bat (creates a virtual environment and installs dependencies) or use the EXE built by build.bat. Updates are never installed automatically; the update check is off until you enable it and give a feed URL.

faq.q: Does the app keep my downloads?
faq.a: No. After publishing (or failing/cancelling) the job's temporary folder is deleted. The database stores metadata only.

faq.q: Why is a file over 50 MB rejected?
faq.a: Bale bots can upload at most 50 MB per file through the Bot API. Enable 'split large files' for 49 MB parts.
Yes, in the Add-links dialog. The app starts the job at the chosen time because the Bale API has no scheduling.
It is stored in the Windows Credential Manager and masked everywhere. Never share it.
Only users in the Users list. Everyone else gets a short 'not authorised' reply with their numeric ID.

faq.q: Why can't I download from a private IP?
faq.a: Blocking localhost/private addresses (SSRF) protects your network.

faq.q: Why did the channel test post a message?
faq.a: It is the only way to verify posting rights; the message is deleted immediately.
Through yt-dlp for public content that is allowed. DRM, logins and paywalls are not supported.

faq.q: What happens if the PC crashes?
faq.a: On restart unfinished jobs return to the queue and resume if possible; orphan files are cleaned.
Settings → Appearance: Persian (RTL), English, Chinese – switch any time.
